comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C3 regarding NEKL-3-mediated phosphorylation of OSM-3 at the elbow region. Both evaluations find the evidence well-supported through in vitro assays, mass spectrometry, and structural modeling. Reviewers explicitly affirm these findings as robust.

Strong agreement on claims C5-C6, C44-C51 regarding in vitro biochemical evidence. Both evaluations support that PD mutation increases ATPase activity, gliding speed, and processivity, while PM mutation shows modest effects. Reviewers describe the work as 'well performed' with results supporting conclusions.

Agreement on claims C7-C9, C26-C30 regarding in vivo phenotypes. Both evaluations support the distinct localization patterns and ciliary defects of PD and PM mutants. Peer review includes C28, C31-C32 which OpenEval addresses separately. Both find evidence robust through genetic data and imaging.

Perfect agreement on claims C38-C43 regarding structural modeling. Both evaluations support the AlphaFold2 predictions and energy minimization analyses. OpenEval notes these are computational predictions benefiting from experimental validation, while peer reviewers accept the approach without challenge.

Strong agreement on claims C52-C58, C69-C70 regarding genetic suppressor evidence. Both evaluations support the A489T suppressor mutation findings and restoration of function. Peer review also includes C57, C97-C98 which OpenEval addresses separately in R7. Both treat this as key confirmatory evidence.

Agreement on claims C57, C97-C98 regarding T489 mutant phenotypes. OpenEval supports that both T489E and T489A recapitulate hyperactive phenotype, indicating dynamic phosphorylation cycling is necessary. Peer review groups these claims with the broader suppressor analysis (R5).

Divergent evaluation on claims C34-C35, C59-C60, C63, C72 regarding mechanistic model. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative elements (phosphatase identity, dephosphorylation location). Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretive model as a 'compelling contribution' without expressing uncertainty about undemonstrated mechanisms.

Agreement on claims C37, C73-C76 regarding dual phosphorylation sites. Both evaluations support the integration of findings from the companion study (Huang et al., 2025). OpenEval explicitly notes citation support, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the framework without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C88-C89, C91-C94 regarding mechanistic explanation for assay differences. Both evaluations support the interpretation that gliding vs. single-molecule assays probe different regulatory aspects. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this explanation without questioning the PM mutant behavior.

Partial overlap on claims C10, C31-C33. OpenEval evaluates the regulatory mechanism inference as SUPPORTED by combined in vitro/in vivo data. Peer review R3 focuses on in vivo phenotypes (C7-C9, C26-C32) and rates as SUPPORTED. Both agree on the evidence quality but group claims differently.

Minimal overlap on claim C33 regarding phosphorylation as regulatory mechanism. OpenEval R4 rates C33 as SUPPORTED based on experimental evidence. Peer review R6 incorporates C33 into broader mechanistic model (C33-C35, C59-C60, C63, C72) and rates as SUPPORTED despite speculative elements.

Agreement on claims C84-C85 regarding broader implications for kinesin regulation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the generalization is speculative and requires validation in other kinesins. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating this as a significant conceptual advance without expressing uncertainty about the generalization.

Minimal overlap on claim C10 regarding novel regulatory mechanism. OpenEval R4 evaluates C10 with C31-C33 as SUPPORTED regulatory inference. Peer review R9 groups C10 with C23, C84-C85 as broader conceptual advance, rating as SUPPORTED. Both agree on significance but differ in scope.

Minimal overlap on claim C23 regarding knowledge gap. OpenEval R13 evaluates background claims C4, C20-C23 as SUPPORTED for framing study novelty. Peer review R9 incorporates C23 into evaluation of broader significance (C10, C23, C84-C85). Both support the claim but in different contexts.

Minimal overlap on claim C28 regarding comparison to G444E mutant. OpenEval R10 evaluates C28, C66-C68 as SUPPORTED for disposal mechanism with caveat that direct demonstration is pending. Peer review R3 includes C28 in broader in vivo phenotype evaluation without specifically addressing disposal mechanism.

OpenEval evaluates claims C86-C87, C95-C96 regarding protein preparation and SEC-MALS characterization as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C11-C19, C24-C25 regarding background information and biological context as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C36-C37, C61-C62, C64-C65, C71-C72, C77-C83 regarding additional regulatory mechanisms and future directions as UNCERTAIN, noting many are speculative hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this collection of speculative claims.

OpenEval evaluates claim C90 regarding correlation between ATPase activity and structural states as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this validation claim.
OpenEval evaluates claim C99 regarding OSM-3 and NEKL-3 localization in soma and dendrites as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this localization observation.
